title: Three permanent works at the consummation: the shining ground, the binding of the proprium, and the fixed separation
reading:
At the close of regeneration three works are established in the soul, and these three, once made, have no end. They begin in light, and unlike everything else within the soul they will not pass; they have no other shape they could be turned into and no terminus at which they would cease willing to be. They stand because in them the proprium is finally bound — that which had stood up against the light from the beginning is now held fast inside its own bound, and cannot rise again.

The first work is the new ground of the natural mind, which itself now sheds light. The natural that had once been claimed and turned dark is set as a luminous earth: a regenerated substrate, fixed and shining, established as the ordered field upon which everything else of the soul will rest. What had been an alien body laid upon it has been turned away; the ground itself now gives forth the light it had only borrowed before.

The second work is the quenching of the fire that had belonged to self-love — the beam by which the proprium had cast its glare across the natural. The devouring love that had counterfeited light is put out at its source, so that nothing in the new ground burns with the old heat any longer.

The third work is the desolation of all that had set itself in its own works — those self-loves which had appropriated what flowed through them and made of it their own deed. Each is now set apart according to the bitter works it had done, and each is fixed upon the proprium that had once exalted itself against the Lord. They are gathered into the last bolos at the moment when into that place is poured the likeness of every form that cannot be raised — every image the proprium had generated of itself. There they are bound together in the last bond forever, sealed as a pit of embers, as gloom, as shadow without measure: the prison the proprium has made of itself by its own claiming.

And between this gathered, sealed mass and the soul that has come into the light, the Lord sets a great boundary with a strong guard, so that the two states can never again strike at each other, never again hear each other's voice, but stand at the greatest distance, fully separated, forever and ever. What is the Lord's is the Lord's; what was claimed and could not be laid off is held away in its own place; and the two are no longer mingled, no longer near, no longer able to disturb one another.
